### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via getObject (literal, a string literal in DataEngineLike))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via IObjectQLEngine (symbol, a top-level interface), judgeFilter (literal, a string literal in DataEngineLike))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 70 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 327391c3af452fd8b2d2b6db9774cf7eca6cd4a1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3c695f419856df5aea17f25bee29a28fe000b245` — the merge of head `82c4552cbfcf9cf977ee26b020bdefaf8e8a9973` into base `327391c3af452fd8b2d2b6db9774cf7eca6cd4a1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3c695f419856df5aea17f25bee29a28fe000b245 && git checkout 3c695f419856df5aea17f25bee29a28fe000b245
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 327391c3af452fd8b2d2b6db9774cf7eca6cd4a1 82c4552cbfcf9cf977ee26b020bdefaf8e8a9973 && git checkout -B drift-repro 327391c3af452fd8b2d2b6db9774cf7eca6cd4a1 && git merge --no-ff 82c4552cbfcf9cf977ee26b020bdefaf8e8a9973

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 327391c3af452fd8b2d2b6db9774cf7eca6cd4a1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 327391c3af452fd8b2d2b6db9774cf7eca6cd4a1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `82c4552cbfcf9cf977ee26b020bdefaf8e8a9973`
Local-runs: none

Review of PR #21170 (card #21080), rendered on the head above from the card and every comment on it, the two cross-lane notes (`5929847116`, `5929854893`) and their answers, the PR body and file list, the three-dot diff against the merge base `bafb8c9498` (16 files, +762 / −2), and the check-runs on the head. ⚠️ Classes and positions only. ⛔ The dispatch order and the seat's conclusions were not inputs; where this record agrees with the ACCEPT `5931764832` it is by independent reading.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged.

1. **`@objectstack/spec` — `IObjectQLEngine.hasObjectMiddleware?(objectName): boolean`** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts`, beside `registerMiddleware`). Optional, declaration and docblock only; the docblock states the probe spelling its one consumer uses. Right: an optional member compiles for every implementer, and the consumer's "cannot say" tier is what makes optionality safe.
2. **`@objectstack/objectql` — `ObjectQL.hasObjectMiddleware`** (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, beside `registerMiddleware`). It reads `this.middlewares` and nothing else; that array has ONE writer in the file (`registerMiddleware`'s push), so the accessor reads exactly what registration records. Its exclusion (no `object`, or the wildcard) is the exact complement of the two global arms of the dispatch matcher in `executeWithMiddleware`, so what it counts is what the chain keys by object. It runs no middleware and registers none; pinned (`engine-has-object-middleware.test.ts`, 4 cases incl. a positive dispatch control). Global registrations excluded deliberately: right, by triage's ruling (`5925681388`) and by construction — a global middleware is not a gate an object carries by name, and counting the stock boot's eight would decline every object.
3. **`@objectstack/service-analytics` — `DatasetScopedStrategyContext.hasObjectMiddleware?`** (`strategies/types.ts`) and **`AnalyticsServiceConfig.hasObjectMiddleware?`** (`analytics-service.ts`). Both optional and additive. The config member sits outside the claim's named region ("context construction sites"); judged right — the service has no other channel to the engine's answer, and it mirrors `judgeFilter`'s shape one member above it. `AnalyticsService` passes it through untouched, `undefined` included.
4. **`NativeSQLStrategy.canHandle` — the decline** (`strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts`, `readsObjectWithEngineMiddleware`). The native strategy's accept-set narrows by (a) every query whose read set contains an object the hook answers `true` for and (b) every query when the hook answers `undefined`. Right, and placed with the strategy's own precedent declines (#7598, #20887), before anything compiles.
   - **The read set.** With a read-scope provider wired the set is `readScopedObjects`, which `callCtx` derives ONCE as `queryObjects`: the cube's base object, every declared join, and every object a relationship path reaches from any position `namedQueryFields` reads — dimensions, time dimensions, measures, `where` leaves, a measure's own filter, the dataset's own filter, and order keys. That is the same set the object-level admission (#20933) and the read scopes read, so no object the statement reads escapes the decline without also escaping the admission; the decline is exactly as wide as the door's gate. The plugin always wires `getReadScope` (a per-call resolver, answering `undefined` when no security service exists), so on the plugin path `readScopedObjects` is always present. The fallback (base object plus declared joins, as `crossFieldComparisonIn` reads them) is reached only by a context a HOST built without `getReadScope`, where a relationship-path hop onto a gated object is not asked — a residual confined to the hand-built tier, named in ③.
   - **The `!cube` return.** `canHandle` already returns `false` for a query naming no cube (its first line), and a query naming an unregistered cube fails `callCtx`'s own cube-existence gate before any strategy is selected, so the helper's `!cube` return cannot produce a served query. Right.
5. **Every door reaches the hook.** `resolveStrategy` has exactly two callers, `query()` and `generateSql()`, and both build their context with `callCtx`, which spreads `baseCtx` (where the hook lives). `queryDataset`, both the live and the draft-preview branch, runs `DatasetExecutor`, which calls `query()` on a scoped service. So the dataset doors, the direct query door and the SQL echo door all carry the hook. Right.
6. **The declined query reaches the engine with the caller's context.** `ObjectQLStrategy` (priority 20, next after native at 10) calls `executeAggregate(object, …, context)`; the plugin's auto-bridge forwards `context` to `engine.aggregate`; the engine builds its operation context with `operation: 'aggregate'` and the merged caller context and runs `executeWithMiddleware`. The three read gates (`comment-access-hooks.ts`, `activity-read-visibility.ts`, `attachment-access-hooks.ts`) register with an `object` key and their read-operation sets include `count` and `aggregate`. Pinned at the service tier (context identity on the bridge, `engine-middleware-decline.test.ts`) and on a real org-bound boot (`analytics-engine-middleware-objects.dogfood.test.ts`: restricted member equals the data door for comment threads, activity rows and attachments; admin control carries more). Right.
7. **Fail closed, by tier.** Plugin tier: no engine, or an engine without the member, answers `undefined`, the strategy declines every object, the ObjectQL strategy serves them through the engine, and the plugin says so once at `warn`. Right, and the stock boot is not in that tier: the `"data"` service is the `ObjectQL` instance, which carries the member. Hand-built tier: a host that constructs `AnalyticsService` with `executeRawSql` and no hook keeps the native path and is told once at construction. Judged in ③.3.
8. **Census and side effect.** Four object-keyed read-side registrations on the stock boot (comment threads, activity rows, attachments; approval requests via the snapshot redaction) leave the native path; two write-only middleware objects leave it as a side effect, because a registration does not declare its operation. No shipped dataset or dashboard reads any of the six. The side effect is a fast-path cost on two small system objects, not a correctness change. Right, per the ruling ("correctness wins over speed for gated objects").
9. **The approval snapshot redaction** is object-keyed (its registration names the approval request object), so the ruling's "if anything is served, it registers for the objects it redacts" is met by construction and its registration is untouched. Its remaining gap (it runs on `find`/`findOne` only) is not this card's mechanism: ③.5.
10. **Six plugin-level suites' engine doubles gain the member answering `false`.** They model the engine they stand in for; without it they measured the fail-closed tier (22 tests served → refused), which has its own pin. Right.
11. **The SQL echo door on a gated object** is now rendered by `ObjectQLStrategy.generateSql`, which refuses the same set `execute()` refuses (the two are built to accept and reject the same envelope). Covered by the declared narrowing in ②, not a second one.
12. **Check-runs on the head** (read at 2026-10-01T13:05Z): 35 of 35 completed — 32 `success`, 3 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke: path-filtered or opt-in), 0 failed. Green among them: Test Core (6 shards and the gate), TypeScript Type Check (source gates, workspace, consumer gates — the job that runs spec `check:api-surface` — and the debt ledger), Lint & Repo Gates (the roster, `check:adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` included), Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate (3 shards and the gate), Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard (the file list touches no governed surface), and the five card/claim consistency checks. These conclusions are the gate verdicts; the one family the dev could not run locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, which needs a whole-repo build) is CI's to answer, and every CI job on this head is green.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/21080-native-sql-engine-middleware-decline.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/objectql: minor`, `@objectstack/service-analytics: minor`. All three publish (17.5.0, none private). Spec at `minor` is right: an optional member on a published contract interface is an additive API, which `patch` would understate. ObjectQL at `minor` is right: a new public method on `ObjectQL`. Service-analytics at `minor` is right: a new optional config member plus a measured narrowing, shipped as `minor` with the BREAKING banner under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major`; precedents `20051`, `19922`).
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`** — line 2 of the PR body and the same line in the changeset body. Grammar: `yes`, because the published `IObjectQLEngine` face widens by one optional member (and two additive members ride with it), plus ONE arm from the closed pair. `yes` takes at least `minor`: met on all three. `(narrowing)` is BREAKING: the banner is present and names the class newly refused — a query on a gated object that the ObjectQL strategy cannot serve, refused with that strategy's existing `INVALID_FIELD` / `400`, the measured instance being a relationship-path dimension with a non-recombinable measure; on an engine that cannot say, for every object. The multi-hop-dimension arm of the same planner refusal falls in the same declared class. The changeset carries its migration ("What to do after upgrading": the two host actions). Right.
- **ADR-0087 marker**: exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category the gate's `CATEGORIES` lists; its argument holds — no authorable key, spelling, value domain or stored shape moves, the refusal is at request time by an existing envelope, and the declaration changes are additive. Right.
- **Generated artifacts**: the spec change is one interface member in `src/contracts`; the dev reports spec `check:generated` exit 0 and CI's typecheck job, which runs the spec gates, is read in ①.12.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry, answered.

1. **Open question (1), push order** — the order's security clause (push nothing until pins, fix and ablation are done) over push-each-step. Answered: accepted. The history is still legible — pins red at `5c6d445e3a`, fix at `bae287b92e`, changeset at `e74617add7`, then the merge of `main`.
2. **Open question (2), the config member outside the named region** — answered: accepted, judged right in ①.3.
3. **Open question (3), the six test doubles** — answered: accepted, ①.10. **The hand-built tier (surface note, and the seat's explicit question):** a host that wires `executeRawSql` by hand and no hook stays on the native path with a one-time construction warning, which is fail-open for that composition. Judged ACCEPTABLE for this fix, with the residual named, because: (a) the order's fail-closed clause named an engine without the member, and the plugin — the ONLY in-repo composition — implements exactly that; (b) the repo holds no hand-built construction that wires raw SQL (the README's direct-construction example wires no `executeRawSql`, so it never reaches the native strategy and the warning does not even fire for it); (c) in that tier "decline" has no safe fallback by construction — a host that wired raw SQL alone has no `executeAggregate`, so declining would be an outage, not a gate — and the tier is loud (warned at construction) and prescribed in the changeset's upgrade text; (d) the asymmetry (a hook answering `undefined` declines; no hook does not) is deliberate and pinned as a control. Residual: an out-of-repo host that wires raw SQL from an engine holding object-keyed gates and ignores the construction warning; such a host also loses relationship-path hops from the decline's read set when it wires no `getReadScope` (①.4). **README** (`service-analytics/README.md`): its direct-construction prose lists the config-only members and omits this one, as it already omits `judgeFilter`; a docs follow-up for the lane, not a landing condition — the example itself is not on the vulnerable path.
4. **Open question (4), `main` moved after the gate run and was not re-merged** — answered: accepted for review. The PR is mergeable per REST, the three newer commits share no file with this diff, and the head's check-runs (①.12) are the gate reading for this head. Note for landing: the ACCEPT holds this PR in draft until #21156's PR lands and then re-merges `main`; a re-merge yields a NEW head, and this record names only `82c4552cbf…` — the patch-id check the ACCEPT names, or a fresh record, is what carries the verdict across.
5. **Out-of-scope finding (a), security, measured** — the approval snapshot redaction and the activity field-value redaction run on `find`/`findOne` only, so a grouped aggregate over those objects carries a value the data plane masks, on the generic data door and on the analytics door before AND after this PR. This PR neither causes nor widens it: the value was carried natively before and is carried through the engine path after; the gap is in the two redactions' operation sets (`payload-redaction-middleware.ts`, `activity-field-redaction.ts`). **Carrier judged sufficient, conditionally:** #21154 is in flight and its triage ruling `5929903631` directs that claim to measure "the grouping and aggregate arm" and "the approval payload snapshot column on its own generic door" and to fold the family if measured; the seat's ACCEPT `5931764832` commits to filing a card if #21154 does not fold it. Because the fold is conditional and the readings sit in this dispatch's private scratch, the obligation that keeps this from falling through is the seat's: hand the reading to #21154's dev, and file when #21154's report lands without the fold. Not a condition on this PR.
6. **Out-of-scope (b), the read audit records no row for aggregate reads** (an `afterFind` hook) — an observation with no measured reach; recorded, nothing for this PR.
7. **NOT MEASURED: PostgreSQL.** The decline runs before any SQL compiles and reads an engine fact, so it is driver-independent; the path it routes to is the existing engine path. CI's live PG + MySQL conformance job is read in ①.12. Acceptable.
8. **NOT MEASURED: a second-organization member with rows of its own (H3).** The organization wall rides the security service's read filter on both paths and is untouched by this diff; not this card's mechanism. Recorded.
9. **NOT MEASURED locally: the whole dogfood suite** — CI's Dogfood Regression Gate shards are read in ①.12.
10. **Global registrations (eight on the stock boot)** are outside the ruling by its own words; the one the ruling named (approvals) proved object-keyed. Nothing further for this card.
11. **Cross-lane.** `domain:spec` seat 2 acknowledged on the card (`5930662225`, no objection). `domain:engine` (#20966) did not answer `5929847116`, and no objection reached the card within the hour the note set, or since: cleared by the note's own terms, recorded as absence, not consent. The engine-side change is one read-only accessor; the chain, registration and `executeWithMiddleware` are byte-identical.
12. **Other open PRs in the same files** (#21144 in `engine.ts` and `analytics-service.ts`, other regions): whichever lands second merges `main` and re-runs its pins, as the claim says.
13. **Disclosure discipline:** the PR body, the changeset, the three pin files and this record name doors, caller classes, objects, files, functions, codes and statuses; the readings and the probe files stayed private.
